passages.text: Now the word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai, saying, “Get up! Go to the great city of Nineveh and preach against it, because its wickedness has come up before Me.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jonah.
Jonah was the son of Amittai.
The LORD gave Jonah a command.
The LORD said, "Get up."
The LORD said, "Go to Nineveh."
Nineveh was a great city.
The LORD said, "Preach against Nineveh."
The LORD said, "Their wickedness has come up before Me."
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר־ יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־ יוֹנָ֥ה בֶן־ אֲמִתַּ֖י לֵאמֹֽר׃ ק֠וּם לֵ֧ךְ אֶל־ נִֽינְוֵ֛ה הָעִ֥יר הַגְּדוֹלָ֖ה וּקְרָ֣א עָלֶ֑יהָ כִּֽי־ עָלְתָ֥ה רָעָתָ֖ם לְפָנָֽי׃

passages.text: Jonah, however, got up to flee to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD. He went down to Joppa and found a ship bound for Tarshish. So he paid the fare and went aboard to sail for Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Jonah was the son of Amittai.
The LORD spoke to Jonah.
Jonah tried to escape from the LORD.
Jonah got up and left.
He wanted to go to Tarshish.
He wanted to get away from the presence of the LORD.
Jonah went down to Joppa.
He found a ship going to Tarshish.
Jonah paid the fare for the ship.
He went aboard the ship.
He planned to travel with the others to Tarshish.
Jonah was still trying to escape from the presence of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיָּ֤קָם יוֹנָה֙ לִבְרֹ֣חַ תַּרְשִׁ֔ישָׁה מִלִּפְנֵ֖י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּ֨רֶד יָפ֜וֹ וַיִּמְצָ֥א אָנִיָּ֣ה׀ בָּאָ֣ה תַרְשִׁ֗ישׁ וַיִּתֵּ֨ן שְׂכָרָ֜הּ וַיֵּ֤רֶד בָּהּ֙ לָב֤וֹא עִמָּהֶם֙ תַּרְשִׁ֔ישָׁה מִלִּפְנֵ֖י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Then the LORD hurled a great wind upon the sea, and such a violent storm arose that the ship was in danger of breaking apart.
passages.sermon:
The LORD acted with power.
The LORD sent a great wind onto the sea.
A violent storm arose on the sea.
The ship was in danger.
The ship was about to break apart.
passages.original: וַֽיהוָ֗ה הֵטִ֤יל רֽוּחַ־ גְּדוֹלָה֙ אֶל־ הַיָּ֔ם וַיְהִ֥י סַֽעַר־ גָּד֖וֹל בַּיָּ֑ם וְהָ֣אֳנִיָּ֔ה חִשְּׁבָ֖ה לְהִשָּׁבֵֽר׃

passages.text: The sailors were afraid, and each cried out to his own god. And they threw the ship’s cargo into the sea to lighten the load. But Jonah had gone down to the lowest part of the vessel, where he lay down and fell into a deep sleep.
passages.sermon:
The sailors saw the storm.
The sailors became afraid.
Each sailor cried out to his own god.
The sailors threw the cargo into the sea.
They did this to make the ship lighter.
Jonah went down to the lowest part of the ship.
Jonah lay down there.
Jonah fell into a deep sleep.
passages.original: וַיִּֽירְא֣וּ הַמַּלָּחִ֗ים וַֽיִּזְעֲקוּ֮ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־ אֱלֹהָיו֒ וַיָּטִ֨לוּ אֶת־ הַכֵּלִ֜ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּֽאֳנִיָּה֙ אֶל־ הַיָּ֔ם לְהָקֵ֖ל מֵֽעֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְיוֹנָ֗ה יָרַד֙ אֶל־ יַרְכְּתֵ֣י הַסְּפִינָ֔ה וַיִּשְׁכַּ֖ב וַיֵּרָדַֽם׃

passages.text: The captain approached him and said, “How can you sleep? Get up and call upon your God. Perhaps this God will consider us, so that we may not perish.”
passages.sermon:
The captain of the ship saw Jonah.
The captain went to Jonah.
The captain spoke to Jonah.
The captain said, “Why are you sleeping?”
The captain said, “Get up.”
The captain said, “Call to your God.”
The captain said, “Maybe your God will notice us.”
The captain said, “Maybe we will not die.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרַ֤ב אֵלָיו֙ רַ֣ב הַחֹבֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ מַה־ לְּךָ֣ נִרְדָּ֑ם ק֚וּם קְרָ֣א אֶל־ אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אוּלַ֞י יִתְעַשֵּׁ֧ת הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים לָ֖נוּ וְלֹ֥א נֹאבֵֽד׃

passages.text: “Come!” said the sailors to one another. “Let us cast lots to find out who is responsible for this calamity that is upon us.” So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
passages.sermon:
The sailors spoke to each other.
They said, “Come, let us cast lots.”
They wanted to find out who caused this trouble for them.
They cast lots.
The lot fell on Jonah.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֞וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־ רֵעֵ֗הוּ לְכוּ֙ וְנַפִּ֣ילָה גֽוֹרָל֔וֹת וְנֵ֣דְעָ֔ה בְּשֶׁלְּמִ֛י הָרָעָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את לָ֑נוּ וַיַּפִּ֙לוּ֙ גּֽוֹרָל֔וֹת וַיִּפֹּ֥ל הַגּוֹרָ֖ל עַל־ יוֹנָֽה׃

passages.text: “Tell us now,” they demanded, “who is to blame for this calamity that is upon us? What is your occupation, and where have you come from? What is your country, and who are your people?”
passages.sermon:
The sailors spoke to Jonah.
They demanded answers from him.
They said, “Tell us now.”
They asked, “Who is to blame for this disaster that has come upon us?”
They asked, “What is your occupation?”
They asked, “Where have you come from?”
They asked, “What is your country?”
They asked, “Who are your people?”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו הַגִּידָה־ נָּ֣א לָ֔נוּ בַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר לְמִי־ הָרָעָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את לָ֑נוּ מַה־ מְּלַאכְתְּךָ֙ וּמֵאַ֣יִן תָּב֔וֹא מָ֣ה אַרְצֶ֔ךָ וְאֵֽי־ מִזֶּ֥ה עַ֖ם אָֽתָּה׃

passages.text: “I am a Hebrew,” replied Jonah. “I worship the LORD, the God of the heavens, who made the sea and the dry land.”
passages.sermon:
Jonah spoke to the sailors.
Jonah said, “I am a Hebrew.”
Jonah said, “I worship the LORD.”
The LORD is the God of the heavens.
The LORD made the sea.
The LORD made the dry land.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם עִבְרִ֣י אָנֹ֑כִי וְאֶת־ יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ אֲנִ֣י יָרֵ֔א אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֥ה אֶת־ הַיָּ֖ם וְאֶת־ הַיַּבָּשָֽׁה׃

passages.text: Then the men were even more afraid and said to him, “What have you done?” The men knew that he was fleeing from the presence of the LORD, because he had told them.
passages.sermon:
The men on the ship became very afraid.
They feared greatly.
They said to Jonah, “What have you done?”
The men knew Jonah was running away from the LORD.
Jonah had told them he was fleeing from the presence of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיִּֽירְא֤וּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁים֙ יִרְאָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֔ה וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו מַה־ זֹּ֣את עָשִׂ֑יתָ כִּֽי־ יָדְע֣וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים כִּֽי־ מִלִּפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ ה֣וּא בֹרֵ֔חַ כִּ֥י הִגִּ֖יד לָהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Now the sea was growing worse and worse, so they said to Jonah, “What must we do to you to calm this sea for us?”
passages.sermon:
Jonah was a Hebrew prophet.
Jonah was on a ship with other men.
A violent storm struck the sea.
The storm became worse and worse.
The men saw the danger.
The men spoke to Jonah.
They asked Jonah a question.
They said, “What must we do to you?”
They wanted the sea to become calm for them.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ אֵלָיו֙ מַה־ נַּ֣עֲשֶׂה לָּ֔ךְ וְיִשְׁתֹּ֥ק הַיָּ֖ם מֵֽעָלֵ֑ינוּ כִּ֥י הַיָּ֖ם הוֹלֵ֥ךְ וְסֹעֵֽר׃

passages.text: “Pick me up,” he answered, “and cast me into the sea, so it may quiet down for you. For I know that I am to blame for this violent storm that has come upon you.”
passages.sermon:
Jonah was a prophet who was fleeing from the presence of the LORD.
A violent storm came upon the sea because of Jonah.
Jonah spoke to the men on the ship.
He said, “Pick me up.
Throw me into the sea.
Then the sea will become calm for you.
I know that I am the reason for this great storm that has come upon you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם שָׂא֙וּנִי֙ וַהֲטִילֻ֣נִי אֶל־ הַיָּ֔ם וְיִשְׁתֹּ֥ק הַיָּ֖ם מֵֽעֲלֵיכֶ֑ם כִּ֚י יוֹדֵ֣עַ אָ֔נִי כִּ֣י בְשֶׁלִּ֔י הַסַּ֧עַר הַגָּד֛וֹל הַזֶּ֖ה עֲלֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Nevertheless, the men rowed hard to get back to dry land, but they could not, for the sea was raging against them more and more.
passages.sermon:
The men were on a ship in a violent storm.
The men tried to row back to dry land.
They rowed with all their strength.
They could not reach the land.
The sea became more and more violent against them.
passages.original: וַיַּחְתְּר֣וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים לְהָשִׁ֛יב אֶל־ הַיַּבָּשָׁ֖ה וְלֹ֣א יָכֹ֑לוּ כִּ֣י הַיָּ֔ם הוֹלֵ֥ךְ וְסֹעֵ֖ר עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: So they cried out to the LORD: “Please, O LORD, do not let us perish on account of this man’s life! Do not charge us with innocent blood! For You, O LORD, have done as You pleased.”
passages.sermon:
The sailors were afraid.
They spoke to the LORD.
They prayed to the LORD.
They said, “LORD, please do not let us die because of this man’s life.
Do not make us guilty for killing an innocent man.
LORD, you have done what you wanted.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרְא֨וּ אֶל־ יְהוָ֜ה וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ אָנָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ אַל־ נָ֣א נֹאבְדָ֗ה בְּנֶ֙פֶשׁ֙ הָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּ֔ה וְאַל־ תִּתֵּ֥ן עָלֵ֖ינוּ דָּ֣ם נָקִ֑יא כִּֽי־ אַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר חָפַ֖צְתָּ עָשִֽׂיתָ׃

passages.text: At this, they picked up Jonah and cast him into the sea, and the raging sea grew calm.
passages.sermon:
The men picked up Jonah.
They threw Jonah into the sea.
The sea stopped raging.
The sea became calm.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׂאוּ֙ אֶת־ יוֹנָ֔ה וַיְטִלֻ֖הוּ אֶל־ הַיָּ֑ם וַיַּעֲמֹ֥ד הַיָּ֖ם מִזַּעְפּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then the men feared the LORD greatly, and they offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made vows to Him.
passages.sermon:
The men saw what happened.
They became very afraid of the LORD.
They felt great fear and respect for the LORD.
They offered a sacrifice to the LORD.
They made vows to the LORD.
passages.original: וַיִּֽירְא֧וּ הָאֲנָשִׁ֛ים יִרְאָ֥ה גְדוֹלָ֖ה אֶת־ יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּֽזְבְּחוּ־ זֶ֙בַח֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וַֽיִּדְּר֖וּ נְדָרִֽים׃

passages.text: Now the LORD had appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah spent three days and three nights in the belly of the fish.
passages.sermon:
The LORD acted with power and authority.
The LORD chose a great fish.
The LORD sent the great fish to swallow Jonah.
Jonah was inside the belly of the fish.
Jonah stayed there for three days.
Jonah stayed there for three nights.
passages.original: וַיְמַ֤ן יְהוָה֙ דָּ֣ג גָּד֔וֹל לִבְלֹ֖עַ אֶת־ יוֹנָ֑ה וַיְהִ֤י יוֹנָה֙ בִּמְעֵ֣י הַדָּ֔ג שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה יָמִ֖ים וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה לֵילֽוֹת׃
